comparator.name: International Development Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: Current BIN handbook: 114 common credits, 24 taught Sociology of Development credits, a 12-credit thesis and 30 open credits. General and fieldwork safety are zero-credit requirements. Thesis entry requires 102 prescribed credits including all first-year courses and mandatory knowledge; this example completes all taught prescribed study, including all four thesis-preparation courses, before the thesis. Dutch-taught full-time bachelor; 2026 entrant route selected by official order.

components.name: Global Challenges and Communication in a Changing World
Academic Skills Journey
components.note: Academic, research and personal development skills and career reflection. General safety is an additional zero-credit requirement.

components.name: Research Methods in the Social Sciences
Critical Perspectives on Agricultural and Rural Development
Economics Evolving: A History of Ideas of Development and Growth
Economic and Sociological Analysis of Rural Livelihoods
Methods, Techniques and Data Analysis for Field Research
components.note: Fieldwork safety is mandatory. Research design, problem analysis and rural-livelihoods study prepare the qualitative and quantitative field-research training.

components.name: Field Research Practical
components.note: Required field research in the Netherlands, England or Ireland: proposal preparation, two weeks of individual fieldwork, then analysis and reporting. Complete fieldwork safety and prepare through the field-methods course.

components.name: Globalization and Sustainability of Food Production and Consumption
The Sociology of Farming and Rural Life
components.note: Complete fieldwork safety. Prior social and development theory and study of agricultural development, political sociology and food globalisation prepare the course.

components.name: Planetary Development: Sociological and Anthropological Perspectives
BSc Thesis Sociology of Development
components.note: Required 12-credit supervised literature-based research project; empirical research may supplement it. Entry requires at least 102 prescribed credits including all first-year courses, plus at least two of the four named specialisation courses. This example completes all prescribed taught courses before the thesis.

components.name: Open electives and/or minor
components.note: Thirty open credits for a minor and/or individual electives at WUR or another university. No particular package or exchange is required.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic target has three equally formal 36-EC specialisations: Sociology of Development, Economics of Development, and Politics and Communication in Development. None is identified as the general route, so the first current handbook specialisation is selected neutrally and independently of UCR fit.

audience.programmeDescription: International Development Studies examines inequality, poverty, livelihoods, food systems and environmental change through sociology, economics, communication, law and governance.
